# PullMark

> PullMark is a free, open-source (MIT) native macOS app that renders local
> Markdown the way readers will see it and reviews documentation-heavy GitHub
> pull requests as rendered diffs with word-level highlights. It is built for
> reading and reviewing the Markdown that coding agents and teams produce:
> plans, specs, design docs, ADRs, runbooks.

Key facts: macOS 13+, signed and notarized, zero telemetry. Installs via
Homebrew (`brew tap jedijashwa/tap && brew trust jedijashwa/tap && brew
install --cask pullmark`) or a DMG from GitHub releases. Authenticates to
GitHub with the credentials already on the system (`gh auth token`, then
`git credential fill`) — it has no login of its own.

Distinctive capability: **margin notes** — review feedback stored in the
Markdown file itself as HTML comments (`<!-- note @name: comment -->`) that
stay out of the rendered page. A person reads a draft rendered, leaves
anchored notes, and tells their agent to "address my notes"; the agent reads
each note in place, applies or answers it, and deletes it. This makes
PullMark a feedback loop for agent-written documents that needs no commit,
no paste-back, and no pull request.

## Docs

- [Review your agent's plans](https://pullmark.app/uses/agents/): the margin-notes
  loop for agent-written drafts, including the instructions snippet to give
  an agent
- [Documentation](https://pullmark.app/docs/): overview of every feature
- [Margin notes](https://pullmark.app/docs/experimental/margin-notes/): the
  note format and behavior in detail
- [Command line](https://pullmark.app/docs/cli/): the `pullmark` command
  (`pullmark plan.md`, `pullmark --diff plan.md`)
- [Troubleshooting](https://pullmark.app/docs/troubleshooting/): GitHub
  access and credential fine print

- [Homepage](https://pullmark.app/)

- [Privacy](https://pullmark.app/privacy/): local-first; fetched PR content
